checks.claim: C1 objects and field identification: same real d1 Riesz/white amplitude and parameters, f and q each nonzero and nonnegative, actual Z, v, signed Y_delta, same residual, potential and F including constants.
checks.reason: Lines 11-34 match target-v1 and tilt Sections 1, 3 and 5. For psi=f tensor q, tilt (5) gives h=k(t)U(x), with U=Gamma*q retaining c_Gamma. From W^delta(u,x)=delta^(a/2)W(delta u,x), the fast-time equation has coefficient sqrt(delta)W(delta u,x)=g W^delta. The tilt s=1/sqrt(delta) adds exactly h(delta u,x), so (1) is the correct retained potential. Y_delta is a continuous scalar of the driver before squaring, and Y_delta^2=J_delta^h.

checks.claim: C1 k and K_par: bounds (5), Lipschitz k, one legal compact K_par, and continuity and positivity of F_psi and I_psi.
checks.reason: |t-s|^-a>=1 on [0,1] gives k>=m_f>0. The integral of |t-s|^-a over s in [0,1] is at most 2/(1-a), which gives the upper bound. Moving the derivative onto the zero-extended f gives |k'|<=2||f'||/(1-a). The example interval contains the range. Ground-family (2),(4) give lambda_b positive, bounded and continuous on K_par, so (6) holds. Constants are selected for this one family only (lines 74-75).

checks.claim: C1 mask, profile and freezing: d_r->0 in (7), admissibility of capped profiles (8), and freezing bound (9).
checks.reason: The decomposition (zeta_r-1)U' + zeta_r'U with |zeta_r'|<=C/r and the tilt C1 tails gives (7), with no L1 assumption and no equality claim for Riesz. The white case is correctly d_r=0 for large r. Profiles (8) are compact, Lipschitz into C_b^1, and have K_base uniform in j, delta and r>=1. Frozen bU is admissible through (5.6) because the tail is C1-vanishing, not compact. In (9), writing (k_bar-b_m)zeta_rU + b_m(zeta_r-1)U with nu+u<=B gives C[delta B+d_r]. The note on used versus full-unit endpoints is in findings.minor.

checks.claim: C2 actual unit control: accepted (7.1)-(7.3) apply to reset physical flows with common W^delta, without growing S(j) constants or independence.
checks.reason: W^delta(j+u,x)=delta^(a/2)W(delta j+delta u,x) is literally W_j^delta(u,x) of (7.1), with the same g and the same mask R_delta=c/delta=r. The conjugation A^h(j+u)-A^h(j)=S(-j)[gM_j(u)+A_(h_j)(u)]S(j) gives P(j+t,j+s)=S(t)U_j(t,s)S(-s), and S(j) cancels exactly. I checked this directly; the note cites it together with tilt Section 5 rather than displaying it. (7.3) is a samplewise consequence of (5.3), so taking epsilon=x_delta on {x_delta<=1} is legitimate. Constants come from unit-horizon bounds only, and no independence is used.

checks.claim: C2 measurable x_delta->0 with correct exponent and finite p, open padding, unchanged actual prefix, and norms of differences only.
checks.reason: (10) is (7.2) with q=p, and its exponent is positive exactly when p>4/(1-a). x_delta is a finite maximum of separable path norms. The padding is disclosed: ceil(L)+1-L<2. Young flows on a prefix depend only on the driver prefix, and k_bar=k up to L, so the observable is unchanged. Lines 155-159 use uniform norms of differences and bounded operator norms, and no norm continuity of S.

checks.claim: C3 noncommuting telescope (12): arbitrary n, correct product order, induction.
checks.reason: I verified n=2 and the inductive split A_nP_A-B_nP_B=B_n(P_A-P_B)+(A_n-B_n)P_A directly. The index order B_(n-1)...B_(k+1)(A_k-B_k)A_(k-1)...A_0 is correct with the earliest factor on the right. The bound n A^(n-1) e_delta follows. No commutation is used.

checks.claim: C3 fixed-B block error (13): uniform A and e_delta, maximum over all blocks and partial times, B not growing, and deterministic freezing proved.
checks.reason: Freezing is derived from (5.5) linearity in h, Lipschitz implies C^theta on the unit horizon, (5.3), and bounded S on [0,1]. Actual norms are at most A through deterministic bound + C_1, and frozen norms through (5.2). At most B unit pieces make up [mB,mB+t], since B and mB are integers. n A^n e<=B A^B e for n<=B, because A>=1 and e>=0. Used times for m=N are restricted to [0,s]. B is chosen before delta. The Riesz defect appears only as the error d_r. Autonomy of frozen P_b is used at line 190 and in (11) without an explicit one-line derivation; it follows from the shift identity of A_(bU). See findings.minor.

checks.claim: C4 terminal extension and full cone premise: N, s, (14)-(15), M_B finite, no new noise, and observed D_N(s) unchanged.
checks.reason: N=floor(L/B) and s=L-NB lies in [0,B). D_N(t)-P(t)=P(t-s)[D_N(s)-P(s)] follows from P(t)=P(t-s)P(s). The case t<=s is absorbed because M_B>=1. For s=0, D_N(0)=I and the extension equals P_(b_N). M_B is finite by (5.2), or by the projection plus complement bound. No operator beyond L enters the extension, and the observed value at s is the actual operator.

checks.claim: C4 the explicit cone-error premise is discharged on measurable event (16), with no desired product conclusion or closeness assumed.
checks.reason: Moving-block (5) requires only b_m in K with consecutive gaps <=omega and sup||D_m(t)-P_(b_m)(t)||<=epsilon. Both are derived: gaps <=Lip(k) delta B, including b_N, and the error <=xi_delta<=epsilon_cone on E_delta. xi_delta is defined as a scalar whether or not x_delta<=1. P(E_delta)->1 follows from (10) plus a_delta(B)->0 at fixed B. The assembly assumes no whole-product closeness or growth.

checks.claim: C5 event (3): cone constants independent of delta, N and s, Y product identification, positive observable, Riemann sum including last interval, and loss and prefactor budgets, with rate I_psi.
checks.reason: (17) is exactly moving-block (7) with T=B and z_(m+1)=D_m(B)z_m. The composition law gives Y=J(D_N(s)...D_0(B)e0). R_delta has weights summing to 1 and left-endpoint samples on intervals of length at most delta B, including the last of length delta s, so |R_delta-I_psi|<=w_F(delta B). 0<=delta(N-1)<=1/B<=1 and log(1-rho)<0 give loss >-e/3, and delta log c_*->0. The three e/3 budgets sum to e. The rate comes from the positive functional J applied to the actual product, not from a proxy or norm growth.

checks.claim: C5 probability, version and source-width quantifiers.
checks.reason: Order of choice: e, then rho, then (B, omega, epsilon_cone, c_*), then delta->0. All statements are per fixed delta on finitely many blocks, using the accepted version construction. There is no pathwise supremum over delta or source widths. (3) is a law statement for each delta under the original P, which is the measure used in (19).

checks.claim: C6 moment bound: same-Z event, union bound and Chebyshev, minus density and raw v/2, and valid squared restriction.
checks.reason: Tilt (10) with s=1/sqrt(delta) gives density exp(-Z/sqrt(delta)-v/(2delta)), so (19) is identity (13) with the correct sign. P(|Z|>delta^(-1/4))<=v delta^(1/2). No independence is used. On the intersection, -Z/sqrt(delta)>=-delta^(-3/4). Y>=exp((I-e)/delta)>0 implies Y^2>=exp(2(I-e)/delta), and this also holds when I-e<0. The integrand of (19) is nonnegative everywhere regardless of the sign of the flow elsewhere, so restriction is valid and (20) holds with exact exponent. The note disclaims a first-moment analogue.

checks.reason: delta log p_delta->0, delta*delta^(-3/4)=delta^(1/4)->0, and letting e->0 gives (21). Tilt (14) with T=t, delta=t^(-kappa), R=t delta gives M_delta<=E|u(t,0)|^2 with unit-mass phi and no R^d loss, and M_delta>0 for small delta by (20). kappa matches direct-event (S).
